paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Nobody in it is a one-man show. Paul keeps the road open and strengthens the disciples (Acts 18:23). Priscilla and Aquila stay put in Ephesus. The brothers write a letter. God's work gets done by a whole kitchen full of people, and every one of them has a different job.

Now look at Apollos. He is eloquent, well versed in the Scriptures, fervent in spirit, and he teaches accurately about Jesus, though he knows only the baptism of John (Acts 18:24-25). Priscilla and Aquila hear him and don't make a scene. They take him aside and explain the way of God more accurately (Acts 18:26). I once pressed a whole batch with a blurry stamp and nobody said a word, so a friend who pulls you aside kindly is a GIFT.

And look at where Apollos goes next. When he resolves to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encourage him and write to the disciples there to welcome him, and on his arrival he is a great help to those who by grace had believed (Acts 18:27). I think a man who was taken aside kindly going on to help so many people is a pretty good picture of what a gentle friend can be part of. So here's your takeaway, baker: stay teachable, and when you see a friend who's missing a piece, correct them gently, because knowing the Word is not about being finished, it's about being willing to keep learning, and being a good friend while you do.
